title: Sessionized Latency Attribution and Dynamic Alert Weights
author: Marcus Liang
release_notes: Adds session-aware latency attribution and an adaptive alert-weighting engine. New dashboard panels for session cohorts and a staged rollout flag; backwards-compatible by default.
description:
Motivation: Long-tail latency incidents often originate from correlated sessions (multi-invocation user flows). Existing per-invocation SLOs and cost labels surface noisy signals and create alert fatigue. This PR introduces a sessionized attribution layer that groups invocations into short-lived sessions, attributes latency/cost across the session boundary, and feeds an adaptive alert-weighting engine that down-weights alerts from low-volume ephemeral sessions and up-weights stable cohorts.

What this PR does (single continuous description): 1) sessionizer: introduced a lightweight session_id derivation (prefer client_session_id if present, fallback to sampled trace_id + sliding-window) to bind consecutive invocations into a session for attribution; 2) attribution engine: computes per-session aggregated metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, token-cost sum, kv-cache hit ratio) and emits rollup metrics with stable labels (session_bucket, route_group) to avoid high-cardinality explosion; 3) dynamic alert weights: new service that consumes session rollups and adjusts alert sensitivity per-route using a decay-based volume model (recent_volume, volatility_score -> weight in [0.1,3.0]); 4) dashboards: new 'Session Cohorts' dashboard with treemap of session latency contributors, session volume timeline, and top-k session fingerprints; 5) tracing/sampling: introduce reservoir sampling for traces keyed by session_bucket and a low-overhead span snapshotted summary that keeps only heavy fields for top-k sessions; 6) rollout controls: feature gate telemetry.session_attribution.enabled (off by default), percent rollout via service config, and a dark-launch mode that emits metrics but does not influence active alerts.

Implementation notes: - Metric names: redwood.session.latency.{p50,p95,p99}, redwood.session.tokens.total, redwood.session.volatility_score, redwood.session.alert_weight - New DB table (timeseries index only) redwood_session_rollups (TTL 30d) - Attribution computes attribution windows with a 60s sliding window and session_bucket classification (fingerprint of prompt/template + route) to keep cardinality bounded - Backpressure: pipeline uses bounded async buffers and non-blocking persistence to keep p99 ingest latency < 1ms overhead based on local perf tests.

Testing and benchmarks: - Unit tests for sessionization edge cases (missing session id, split sessions, clock skew) - Integration tests with the mock-routing harness verifying rollback behavior when the gate is off - Load test: 100k QPS synthetic workload with heavy-session churn showed end-to-end ingest overhead +0.8% and memory delta +3% on a 32GB service instance - Accuracy: in synthetic labeled incidents, attribution recovered the originating session in 92% of cases (T=1000 incidents).

Files changed (high-level): see changed_files below. Notable code: telemetry/sessionizer.go (session derivation), telemetry/rollup_worker.go (aggregation + persistence), alerts/dynamic_weights.go (weight engine + calibration), dashboards/session_cohorts.json (grafana panels), tracing/reservoir_sampler.go (session-keyed reservoir), migrations/20260214_add_session_rollups.up.sql.

Rollout plan: 1) merge to main but keep telemetry.session_attribution.enabled=false; 2) dark-launch for 48h on prod namespace - emits metrics only; 3) enable 5% of traffic for 72h, monitor alert-load, false-positive rate, and metric cardinality; 4) progressive roll to 25/50/100 with emergency kill-switch and automated metric threshold rollback (alerts.alert_weight_unexpected_change).

Why this is different from previous work: existing token-focused telemetry provided per-invocation insights; this adds cross-invocation context (sessions) to reveal correlated causes, drastically improving signal-to-noise for SLO alerts without adding unbounded cardinality.

Notes for reviewers: please pay attention to metric naming, cardinality constraints in rollup_worker.go, and reservoir size defaults (current default 512 per bucket).

review_comments: Aisha Rahman: Nice direction — can you add a brief on how cardinality is controlled in rollups? Concerned about route+prompt fingerprints becoming a problem.

Marcus Liang: Response: we bucket by session_bucket which is a hashed fingerprint limited to 4k buckets by default; also we only persist top-k buckets per minute (configurable). Added comments and tests (rollup_worker.go).
Diego Marquez: Please add an e2e that verifies alerts don't fire when gate is in dark-launch mode.
Marcus Liang: Added integration test mock_harness/session_attr_test.go and a CI job that runs the dark-launch path. CI green after fix.
Lea O'Connor: Suggested lowering reservoir default to 256 for lower-memory customers and expose config. Implemented and tested; left default 512 for now with config override.
Aisha Rahman: Approved after test additions and minor naming nits
